acceptedStack.appearanceImplementation: project-owned direct gsplat acceptance adapter (experimental, non-dimensional)

observations: CUDA 13.0.88 and 13.2.51 both compiled and executed native sm_120 kernels.
Open3D CUDA tensor and legacy CPU TSDF are separate workloads.
COLMAP 4.1.1 is selected because the same fixture produced repeatable non-empty dense fusion; 3.13 did not.
Selected COLMAP sparse is CPU deterministic and selected dense is CUDA.
No Linux display driver or host CUDA toolkit was installed.
compatibilitySpike.selectionBasis: CUDA 13.0 and 13.2 executed native sm_120 kernels plus PyTorch, Open3D and gsplat work; 13.2 matches the driver-advertised generation and selected cu132 wheel.

deferredLimitations: No physical iOS capture, LiDAR, ARKit pose, interruption, thermal or upload-resume evidence was run.
No representative-home or survey-grade accuracy evidence was run; synthetic fixtures cannot establish field accuracy.
No phone, customer or provider data was used.
Direct gsplat remains experimental, non-dimensional, acceptance-only and absent from the production worker.
C8 v2 has no production reconstruction route; the exposure guard requires acceptance-only with routing disabled.
COLMAP 3.13 produced depth and normal maps but a zero-vertex strict PLY after geometric, photometric, relaxed and fresh-workspace diagnosis.
Open3D CUDA tensor evidence does not make its separate legacy CPU TSDF a GPU workload.
Synthetic metres supplied to Open3D were not independently physically validated.
APT indices are not snapshot-pinned; exact base/image/source/lock/package/runtime hashes identify the build.
C8 v1 is byte-for-byte unchanged from the integrated base and was not run.
